newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell operating profits up after exit from defense.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell operating profits up after exit from defense.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp., marking the first quarter since it sold its aerospace and defence businesses, said Monday its operating income rose as all its remaining businesses became more profitable.

The company, which emerged as a primarily commercial electronics firm, reported net income of $179 million, or 82 cents per share, in the first quarter. That was 18 percent higher than the $152 million, or 70 cents per share, in profits from continuing operations in the year-ago period. Sales rose 9 percent to $2.6 billion from $2.4 billion.
Discontinued operations provided $40 million in income in the 1996 first quarter.

Rockwell sold its aerospace and defence businesses to Boeing Co. for $3.2 billion in December to focus on higher growth sectors. The company has annual revenues in excess of $10 billion and nearly 60,000 employees.

Automation, semiconductor systems and avionics and communications now account for 71 percent of Rockwell's sales. Sales from its heavy and light vehicle automotive component systems account for the other 29 percent. International sales account for about 43 percent of total sales.

The electronics business brought in $271 million in earnings, up from $232 million in the 1996 period. Automotive earnings grew to $41 million from $38 million mainly as a result of cost-cutting programmes and higher sales in the light vehicle systems business, Rockwell said.
Automation earnings rose 18 percent to $131 million in the first quarter from $111 million due to an 8 percent increase in sales, mainly in higher margin products.

Avionics & Communications earnings surged 44 percent to $59 million from $41 million as a result of higher sales, improved cost performance in defence avionics and the benefit from last year's restructuring charge to exit several non-strategic product lines.
Semiconductor Systems profits edged up to $81 million from $80 million.
Rockwell's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $62.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
